I’ve been off since it happened—maybe a few weeks? It’s hard to keep track. Sometimes I hear a loud bang in the kitchen, like a pot dropping, and I flinch so hard I drop whatever I’m holding. My hands shake. It’s embarrassing in class. I don’t go near the dishwashing area anymore; the clatter, the sudden sounds—it just gets to me. I’ve stopped eating at the cafeteria too. Something about the noise feels… unsafe.

There are gaps in what I remember. Whole pieces of that night are just gone. I know I made it home, but I don’t know how. People ask, and I can’t tell them. I don’t want to talk about it. I avoid the streets near where it happened. I even changed my route to school.

I got praised last week for my plating—finally got that technique right—but I didn’t feel anything. Just numb. My instructor said I should be proud, but pride feels like a foreign language.

I’m short-tempered lately. Little things—a delayed bus, someone bumping into me—set me off. I didn’t used to be like this. I just want to get back to cooking, but it’s like I’m moving through fog. I don’t know if I’m healing or stuck.

I’ve been struggling since the accident… it’s been over two months now. I was driving home from my night class at culinary school when another car hit me head-on. I don’t remember most of it—like, huge chunks are just… gone. The police said I was lucky to walk away, but I can’t even talk about it without feeling like I can’t breathe.  

If I see a car that looks like the one that hit me, or even hear a sudden screech of tires, I jump—sometimes I actually flinch or drop whatever I’m holding. Last week, a pan clattered in the kitchen and I nearly collapsed. I’ve started skipping certain classes because the route passes near the intersection. I don’t go near my own car anymore either.  

Before all this, I loved cooking—I used to beam when my sauces turned out right. Now, even if my chef instructor praises me, it just… doesn’t feel like anything. I’m always on edge, snapping at classmates over tiny things. One part of me knows I should feel proud or happy sometimes, but that switch is broken. It hasn’t gotten better—just worse—and I can’t keep living like this.
D018-D020_h010.question_b:

It was bad—I wasn’t even driving, just a passenger, but sometimes I can’t remember chunks of it, like my brain just shuts down when I try to recall. I get so irritable, especially during service at culinary school—little things set me off, and I feel guilty after.  

I avoid anything that reminds me of it: won’t ride in cars unless I have to, stopped going to the diner we were headed to. Even when my instructors praised my dish last week, something I worked hard on, I didn’t feel proud or happy—just empty. I know it’s been a few months, and I thought I’d be over it by now. The symptoms started right after the accident and are still here, but I don’t feel like I “fit” PTSD. I just can’t bounce back like I used to.
